answer: Each AI agent must lock a cryptographic bond of tokens in a smart‑contract named Juniper, which records the agent’s public key and a reputation score. When a new agent joins the grove, neighboring agents run a zero‑knowledge proof and a randomly chosen falcon node audits the bond; if duplication is detected, the contract slashes the bonded tokens. Thus an attacker must front the full bond for each fake node and pay the audit fee, turning a Sybil surge into a costly venture.
